newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore foreign workers housed in dumps - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Singapore foreign workers housed in dumps - newspaper.

text.p: More than 100 Bangladeshi workers employed by cleaning contractors on Singapore public housing estates are being housed in rubbish dumps, the Sunday Times reported.
The newspaper said the contractors, engaged by town councils, were housing the workers in rubbish bin centres in the estates.
It found workers living in 18 rubbish dumps in checks of housing estates across the island over three nights.
The newspaper quoted a property agent who specialises in housing foreign workers as saying contractors housed their cleaners in the dumps because it was convenient and free.
"It is very difficult to find housing for foreign workers," T. Devadas was quoted as saying.
The town councils said they conducted monthly spot checks on dumps and sent warning letters to those who were housing workers in them.

A Ministry of Labour spokesman told the newspaper it would cancel the work permits of foreign workers and bar contractors if it received reports from town councils or housing authorities that these workers were not being properly housed.
